Verified with this test program:

```go
package main

import "testing"

func TestReverse(t *testing.T) {
    tests := []struct {
        input    string
        expected string
    }{
        {"hello", "olleh"},
        {"world", "dlrow"},
        {"", ""},
        {"a", "a"},
        {"ab", "ba"},
        {"racecar", "racecar"},
        {"Hello, 世界", "界世 ,olleH"},
        {"😀🌍", "🌍😀"},
    }

    for _, tt := range tests {
        got := Reverse(tt.input)
        if got != tt.expected {
            t.Errorf("Reverse(%q) = %q; want %q", tt.input, got, tt.expected)
        }
    }
}
```

**Edge cases tested:**

| Input | Expected | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `""` (empty string) | `""` | Edge: zero-length |
| `"a"` (single char) | `"a"` | Edge: single element |
| `"ab"` | `"ba"` | Two elements |
| `"racecar"` | `"racecar"` | Palindrome (same forward/backward) |
| `"hello"` | `"olleh"` | Basic ASCII |
| `"Hello, 世界"` | `"界世 ,olleH"` | Multi-byte Unicode (CJK) |
| `"😀🌍"` | `"🌍😀"` | Emoji (surrogate pairs / 4-byte runes) |

All tests pass.
